Final – first to 7 sets |winner = |prize_fund = £5,000,000 |winners_share = £1,000,000 |high_checkout = |prev = [[2026 PDC World Darts Championship|2026]] |next = [[2028 PDC World Darts Championship|2028]] }} The '''2027 PDC World Darts Championship''' (known for sponsorship reasons as the '''2026/27 Paddy Power World Darts Championship'''){{cite web |last=Simpson |first=Will |date=7 August 2026 |title=2026/27 Paddy Power World Darts Championship ticket prices confirmed |url=https://www.pdc.tv/news/2026/august/07/2026-27-paddy-power-world-darts-championship-ticket-prices-confirmed/ |website=Professional Darts Corporation |access-date=9 August 2026}} is a professional [[darts]] tournament that is scheduled to take place from 11 December 2026 to 3 January 2027 at [[Alexandra Palace]] in London, England. The 34th [[PDC World Darts Championship|World Darts Championship]] organised by the [[Professional Darts Corporation]] (PDC), it will be the 20th to be staged at Alexandra Palace, where it will be held in the venue's Great Hall for the first time. The tournament's total prize fund will be £5,000,000, of which the winner will receive £1,000,000. The tournament will feature a 128-player field. The top 32 players in the [[PDC World Rankings]] will be [[Seeding (sports)|seeded]] for the first round. [[Luke Littler]] will be the defending champion, having defeated [[Gian van Veen]] 7–1 in the [[2026 PDC World Darts Championship|2026 final]]. == Overview == === Background === [[File:Great Hall Alexandra Palace - geograph.org.uk - 41020.jpg|thumb|The tournament will be held in [[Alexandra Palace]]'s Great Hall ''(pictured in 2005)'' for the first time.]] The [[Professional Darts Corporation]] (PDC) was established under the World Darts Council name by the managers John Markovic, Tommy Cox and Dick Allix, along with the [[Darts world rankings|world's top 16 players]] in January 1992 as a separate body that [[Split in darts|broke away]] from the [[British Darts Organisation]] (BDO).{{cite web|title=PDC History|url=https://www.dartsworld.com/pdc-history/|work=Darts World|access-date=17 April 2026|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191108184503/https://www.dartsworld.com/pdc-history/|archive-date=8 November 2019}} The [[1994 WDC World Darts Championship|inaugural edition]] of the [[PDC World Darts Championship]] was held from December 1993 to January 1994 at the [[Circus Tavern]] in [[Purfleet]], Essex, England. It was won by [[Dennis Priestley]], who defeated [[Phil Taylor (darts player)|Phil Taylor]] in the final on 2 January 1994.{{cite web |date=3 January 1994 |title=Darts: Priestley is supreme as No 1 rebel |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/darts-priestley-is-supreme-as-no-1-rebel-1397713.html |website=The Independent |access-date=17 April 2026}} Taylor would go on to win the tournament 14 times, adding to his [[BDO World Darts Championship]] wins in [[1990 BDO World Darts Championship|1990]] and [[1992 BDO World Darts Championship|1992]] for a record total of 16 world titles, including eight in a row from 1995 to 2002.{{cite web |last=Mirza |first=Raz |date=23 December 2017 |title=Phil Taylor: The greatest darts player to have ever graced the oche |url=https://news.sky.com/story/luke-littler-wins-second-straight-world-darts-championship-13490124 |website=Sky News |access-date=17 April 2026}} === Format === Under the tournament format introduced in 2026, all 128 players, including the 32 [[Seeding (sport)|seeds]], will enter the tournament in the first round. The matches will be in [[Set (darts)|set]] play format, with the amount of sets required to win a match increasing as the tournament progresses. All non-deciding sets will be played to the best of five [[Leg (darts)|legs]]. In the deciding set, a [[tie-break]] rule will be applied if the set score is 2–2, where the first player to lead by two legs will win the set and the match; if the deciding set reaches 5–5, the winner will be decided by a [[Sudden death (sport)|sudden-death]] leg.{{cite web |date=12 December 2025 |title=World Darts Championship 2026 dates, format, schedule, how to watch and favourites - who can challenge Luke Littler? |url=https://www.skysports.com/darts/news/12040/13474781/world-darts-championship-2026-dates-format-how-to-watch-and-favourites-who-can-challenge-luke-littler |website=Sky Sports |access-date=7 August 2026}} {|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !Round !Best of (sets) !First to (sets) |- |First & second || 5 || 3 |- |Third & fourth || 7 || 4 |- |Quarter-finals || 9 || 5 |- |Semi-finals || 11 || 6 |- |Final || 13 || 7 |} === Ranking === The [[PDC World Rankings]] (known for sponsorship reasons as the [[Werner Co.|Werner]] Rankings Ladder) are calculated on a two-year cycle. Prize money won by players in ranking tournaments are removed from their ranking after 104 weeks, meaning players who participated in the [[2025 PDC World Darts Championship|2025 World Championship]], who did not lose their [[PDC Tour Card]] during the two-year period, will 'defend' their prize money from that event. At the end of the tournament, the prize money won at this tournament will be added and the prize money won at the 2025 tournament will be removed. After the tournament, the top 64 players in the PDC World Rankings will receive a one-year extension on their Tour Card, joined by the [[List of players with a 2026 PDC Tour Card|players who earned two-year Tour Cards in 2026]] who will enter their second year in 2027. Players with two or more years on their Tour Card, who finish outside of the top 64, will lose their Tour Card and see their ranking reset to £0, along with all other players who earned prize money in ranking tournaments without holding a Tour Card.{{cite web |title=PDC Rankings Rules |url=https://www.pdc.tv/rankings/pdc-rankings-rules |website=Professional Darts Corporation |access-date=7 August 2026}}{{cite web |author=Paul Nicholson |author-link=Paul Nicholson (darts player) |date=11 April 2021 |title=Is the PDC Order of Merit a 'fair' world ranking system for darts or is it time for change? |url=https://www.sportinglife.com/darts/news/time-for-ranking-system-to-change/190881 |website=Sporting Life |access-date=7 August 2026}} === Prize money === The prize money breakdown is shown below:{{cite web |last=Phillips |first=Josh |date=31 March 2025 |title=Biggest prize money increase in PDC history confirmed|url=https://www.pdc.tv/news/2025/march/31/biggest-prize-money-increase-pdc-history-confirmed |website=Professional Darts Corporation |access-date=7 August 2026}} {|class="wikitable" style="text-align:center" !colspan=2|Position (no. of players) !Prize money

The top 40 players in the two-year [[PDC World Rankings]] after the [[2026 Players Championship Finals]] qualify automatically, followed by the next 40 highest-ranked players in the one-year [[PDC Pro Tour]] rankings. The remaining 48 places go to various international qualifiers. === International qualifiers === There will be 48 players who qualify for the tournament through international qualifiers. For the first time, players from Africa were granted two guaranteed spots, separated into a Northern African qualifier and a Southern African qualifier. The Trans-Tasman Championship was also introduced to determine a fourth qualification route for Oceania.{{cite web |last=Allen |first=Dave |date=20 April 2026 |title=Trans-Tasman Championship introduced for Oceanic stars |url=https://www.pdc.tv/news/2026/april/20/trans-tasman-championship-introduced-for-oceanic-stars/ |website=Professional Darts Corporation |access-date=22 April 2026}} As of 9 November 2026, 38 players have secured a place at the tournament through an international qualifier. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size: 90%" |+class=nowrap| List of international qualifiers for the 2027 PDC World Darts Championship |- !
